new_statements.quote: In Mazateco the stress falls mechanically on the final syllable of a word (this applies, also, to the nouns already listed) and need not be indicated by any orthographic device. The stressed syllable of a dissyllabic word is noticeably longer in duration than the unstressed one that precedes it. The glides of unstressed syllables may be pronounced with extreme rapidity, so rapidly that it is very hard to hear them.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog final stress = fixed final; Pike states exactly that ('falls mechanically on the final syllable of a word') and adds the length correlate and that stress is predictable/unmarked. The lect is the Huautla de Jiménez dialect ('the dialect represented here being that of Huautla de Jimenez, Oaxaca. The data concerning it were gathered by me in collaboration with Miss Eunice Victoria Pike and Mrs. George Cowan, from 1936-45', file), which is the variety huau1238 denotes.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is automatic (non-contrastive) and falls on the last syllable of every word, including nouns; the stressed final syllable is longer than the preceding unstressed one, and unstressed syllables can be very reduced. Pike therefore leaves stress unmarked in his orthography; tone (four levels) is the contrastive prosodic feature.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the passage read.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; 'mechanically' and 'this applies, also, to the nouns already listed' assert full regularity. (The scope of 'word' with respect to enclitics is not addressed in this passage; Pike & Pike 1947 IJAL, already held by the project, treat enclitics as stressless and grouped with the preceding word.)
new_statements.identity_note: Pike 1948 explicitly describes the Mazateco of Huautla de Jiménez, Oaxaca (Highland Mazatec), data gathered 1936-45 with Eunice V. Pike and Florence Cowan; this is the variety Glottolog huau1238 (Huautla Mazatec) covers, so the statement is about the catalog language, not a sister Mazatec variety.

tone_statements.quote: On recense quatre tons de niveau à Huautla (H, h, M et B : le symbole |h| note le ton mi-haut), trois seulement à San Felipe Jalapa de Díaz (H, M, B), et entre quatre et six tons de contour à Huautla, selon différents descripteurs (HB, BM, HM, Bh, BhM, BhB) – en gras, ceux retenus ici.
tone_statements.translation: Four level tones are recorded at Huautla (H, h, M and B: the symbol |h| notes the mid-high tone), only three at San Felipe Jalapa de Díaz (H, M, B), and between four and six contour tones at Huautla, depending on the describer (HB, BM, HM, Bh, BhM, BhB) - in bold, those retained here.
tone_statements.summary: 4 level tones (H, mid-high, M, L) in two registers + 4-6 contours; lexical root-tone classes; tonal verb inflection.

tone_statements.citation: Léonard, Jean Léo & Julien Fulcrand. 2019. From 'complexity' to 'simplexity': a diasystemic approach of Mazatec inflectional classes. Amerindia 41 (Inflectional class complexity in the Oto-Manguean languages): 199-240. Paris: CNRS-SeDyL.
tone_statements.quote: Mazatec has both level and contour tones. Some dialects have three level tones (Jalapa de Díaz) while others have up to four (Huautla, San Miguel Soyaltepec). The ALFALEIM convention for writing tones is the following: High (/H/) represented with an acute accent (í) Mid-high (/h/) represented with a grave accent (ì) Mid (/M/) which is not represented (i) Low (/L/) represented with an underlining (i)

tone_statements.summary: Mazatec diasystem: 3-4 level tones plus contours (per dialect); Ixcatlán not individually described here.

Tesis de maestría en Lingüística Indoamericana, CIESAS, México. 183 pp. Chapter 2 'Bosquejo gramatical del mazateco de Río Santiago' (pp. 10–39), explicitly 'la variante Huautla de Jiménez
tone_statements.quote: tomando en cuenta esta complejidad del sistema tonal mazateco, tanto a nivel léxico como morfológico (marcas de persona, aspecto y posesión), en la presente investigación se reafirma la existencia de cuatro tonos de nivel y cinco tonos de contorno fonológicos. ... para este trabajo se habla de la existencia de los siguientes tonos de nivel y contorno respectivamente. Tonos de nivel 4 Tono alto 3 Tono semi-alto 2 Tono medio 1 Tono bajo Tonos Descendentes / 43 / (que presenta tres realizaciones diferentes [43], [42] y [41]) / 32 / / 21 / ... Tonos Ascendentes /12/ / 23/
tone_statements.translation: taking into account this complexity of the Mazatec tone system, at both the lexical and the morphological level (person, aspect and possession marking), the present study reaffirms the existence of four level tones and five phonological contour tones. ... this work posits the existence of the following level and contour tones respectively. Level tones: 4 high tone, 3 semi-high tone, 2 mid tone, 1 low tone. Falling tones: /43/ (which has three different realisations [43], [42] and [41]), /32/, /21/ ... Rising tones: /12/, /23/
tone_statements.locator: ch. 6 'Conclusiones generales', pp. 165-167; same inventory in 4.6 p. 126 and 5.9 p. 159; 'secuencia de tonos de nivel' statement in 5.4 p. 131
tone_statements.summary: Four level tones (high 4, semi-high 3, mid 2, low 1) plus five contour tones (43, 32, 21, 12, 23), from minimal quartets and Praat F0 data; contours treated as level sequences; nothing on stress.

tone_statements.quote: (13) Huautla Mazateo has four tonemes and thirteen tone clusters. Change of aspect or of person is often indicated by change of tone. ... 13. Mazatee of Huautla de Jiménez (Pike and Fike 1947, K. Pike 1948} has four levels of tone: 1 (high), 2, 3, 4 (low) ... Tone clusters are frequent. ... A few clusters ocour in stems ... tone.quote: tomando en cuenta esta complejidad del sistema tonal mazateco, tanto a nivel léxico como morfológico (marcas de persona, aspecto y posesión), en la presente investigación se reafirma la existencia de cuatro tonos de nivel y cinco tonos de contorno fonológicos. ... para este trabajo se habla de la existencia de los siguientes tonos de nivel y contorno respectivamente. Tonos de nivel 4 Tono alto 3 Tono semi-alto 2 Tono medio 1 Tono bajo Tonos Descendentes / 43 / (que presenta tres realizaciones diferentes [43], [42] y [41]) / 32 / / 21 / ... Tonos Ascendentes /12/ / 23/
tone.locator: ch. 6 'Conclusiones generales', pp. 165-167; same inventory in 4.6 p. 126 and 5.9 p. 159; 'secuencia de tonos de nivel' statement in 5.4 p. 131
tone.translation: taking into account this complexity of the Mazatec tone system, at both the lexical and the morphological level (person, aspect and possession marking), the present study reaffirms the existence of four level tones and five phonological contour tones. ... this work posits the existence of the following level and contour tones respectively. Level tones: 4 high tone, 3 semi-high tone, 2 mid tone, 1 low tone. Falling tones: /43/ (which has three different realisations [43], [42] and [41]), /32/, /21/ ... Rising tones: /12/, /23/
tone.summary: Four level tones (high 4, semi-high 3, mid 2, low 1) plus five contour tones (43, 32, 21, 12, 23), from minimal quartets and Praat F0 data; contours treated as level sequences; nothing on stress.
